_comment: Declarative SSOT for the internal Bugzilla (5.2) project/lifecycle configuration.
setup-projects.pl converges the installation to this state; verify-projects.py asserts it.
spec_version 3.0.0. The four products are Internal/External per project, and BOTH kinds can
hold either a bug or a requirement - so the issue type CANNOT be derived from the product and
is a per-bug field again.
The installation is live: 178 bugs in 'OptionsEdge - Internal'. cf_issue_type is therefore
OPTIONAL at the database level - Bugzilla has no NULL-able custom field, so creating it writes
the unset sentinel '---' into every existing row and nothing more. New items are required to
carry a type, but that is enforced by the extension at CREATION, not by is_mandatory, which
would also block every future edit of the 178 legacy rows.
Legacy rows with no type are treated as BUG: they are internal engineering bugs, and their
statuses and resolutions are already all BUG-valid, so nothing has to be migrated.
_enforcement_switch_comment: There is deliberately NO 'enforcement enabled' parameter: anyone with tweakparams could
turn one off. The extension derives its state instead, anchored on cf_category - the one
object this design creates. Absent outside a web/API request = never provisioned
(bootstrap, nothing enforced, so checksetup.pl and the provisioner can run). Absent or
structurally damaged during a request = BROKEN: every guarded change is refused until

_comment: OPTIONAL at the database level, REQUIRED on creation by the extension. That split is the
whole point: is_mandatory would also apply to every future edit of the 178 pre-existing
rows, which have no type and must stay editable.
An item with no type is treated as BUG (see enforcement.legacy_untyped_is).
OPTIONAL and uncontrolled: one flat BUG_*/REQ_* vocabulary that the extension checks against
the item's issue type. An empty category is always valid, which is what leaves the 178
pre-existing rows freely editable.
Uncontrolled. It used to be tied to the BUG products, but Internal/External no longer means
bug-versus-requirement, so there is no product set it belongs to.

_statuses_comment: The BUG branch keeps Bugzilla's stock names. Renaming CONFIRMED/IN_PROGRESS would be an
UPDATE against the 80 live bugs sitting on them (Field/Choice.pm:158), which the no-touch
constraint forbids. Only the four REQ_* statuses are new, so no bug's status value is
The REQ_ prefix still makes a cross-branch status obvious to a human; the extension is what
makes it impossible. Existing sortkeys are kept exactly as they are (100/200/300/400/500) so
no existing row is rewritten; the new REQ_* statuses take 600-900.
'exists' records which statuses are expected to be there already - the provisioner refuses
to CREATE one marked true, because that would mean the installation is not what we think.
_workflow_comment: Installation-wide matrix (bug_status + status_workflow are global in Bugzilla - there is no
per-product or per-type workflow). Both lifecycles live in this one matrix; the
IssueTypeWorkflow extension is what stops an item crossing between the two branches.
'' (empty from) is the bug-creation row (status_workflow.old_status IS NULL).
Every status must be able to reach duplicate_or_move_bug_status (RESOLVED), otherwise
Bugzilla::Status::add_missing_bug_status_transitions() re-adds the row behind our back.
Rewriting status_workflow does NOT touch bug rows.
_enforcement_comment: Mirrored as Perl constants in extensions/IssueTypeWorkflow/Extension.pm, which the
provisioner refuses to run against if the two disagree. The constants exist so that an
unreadable or half-written config file can never silently turn enforcement off.

_initial_statuses_comment: Every status an item of this type may be CREATED in. initial_status above is the
DEFAULT - what an item falls back to when the reporter had no say, which is the
normal case for an external reporter: Bug.pm:1526-1536 forces UNCONFIRMED for
anyone without editbugs/canconfirm, and for a REQUIREMENT that would land it on
the BUG lifecycle. CONFIRMED is here because it is how this installation has
always worked: of the 178 bugs that predate this work, 78 were filed straight
into CONFIRMED and never moved. Removing that was a regression, not a policy.
_error_codes_comment: illegal_change (115) is core Bugzilla's, raised whenever the extension denies an UPDATE via
priv_results; REST maps it to HTTP 401. The 1000xx codes are the extension's own, registered
through the webservice_error_codes hook and mapped to HTTP 400.

_component_owner_comment: default_assignee is declared here rather than passed on the command line, so two runs with
different arguments cannot produce two different installations from the same SSOT.
--default-assignee remains as the fallback for a component that does not name one.
_products_comment: These four already exist, created by separate work, with 178 live bugs in id 1. They are
adopted as they are. Each is gated by its own group (entry + MANDATORY membercontrol), and
the internal group grants membership of the external one - so internal users see both, and
external users see only external. That access model is NOT managed here; it is recorded so a
reader knows why filing needs group membership.
Both Internal and External can hold bugs AND requirements; the type is cf_issue_type.
